description: A comprehensive study of the generation, transmission, distribution, and protection of electrical energy, including detailed fault analysis and system stability evaluation.

sections.title: Power Generation and Economics
sections.description: Analysis of variable load on power stations and the key economic factors that influence the cost of electrical energy generation.

equations: Load Factor: LF = Average Load / Maximum Demand
Diversity Factor: DF = Sum of Individual Max Demands / Maximum Demand on Power Station
Plant Capacity Factor: PCF = Actual Energy Produced / (Plant Capacity * Hours)

results: Load Factor is always less than 1; higher values indicate a lower cost of generation per unit.
Diversity Factor is always greater than 1; a higher diversity factor means lesser installed capacity is required, reducing capital cost.

sections.title: Transmission Line Parameters and Performance
sections.description: Evaluating the resistance, inductance, and capacitance of transmission lines and understanding their impact on overall line performance.

key_concepts.explanation: A phenomenon in medium and long transmission lines under no-load or light-load conditions where the receiving end voltage becomes greater than the sending end voltage, primarily due to the line's charging current (capacitance).

The ionization of air surrounding the power conductors under high voltage, resulting in a luminous violet glow, hissing noise, and production of ozone gas. It leads to power loss and radio interference.

The tendency of alternating current (AC) to concentrate near the outer surface of a conductor, effectively reducing the cross-sectional area and increasing the effective resistance. It is more pronounced at high frequencies and in solid conductors with large diameters.

sections.title: Fault Analysis
sections.description: Calculating short-circuit currents for symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults occurring in power systems and applying Fortescue's Theorem.

key_concepts.explanation: A mathematical method used to resolve an unbalanced 3-phase system into three sets of balanced components: Positive sequence, Negative sequence, and Zero sequence components.

results: These faults are very rare (accounting for roughly 5% of all faults).
They are the most severe faults, causing maximum mechanical and thermal stress on system equipment.
Analysis requires only the positive sequence network.
Line-to-Ground (LG) fault is the most frequently occurring fault (accounting for 70-80% of all faults).
Zero sequence currents only flow in faults that involve a connection to the ground (like LG and LLG faults).

sections.title: Power System Stability
sections.description: The ability of interconnected synchronous machines to remain in synchronism after being subjected to various disturbances.

key_concepts.explanation: The ability of the power system to maintain synchronism under small and gradual changes in load. The steady-state stability limit is the maximum power that can be transmitted without losing synchronism.

key_concepts.concept: Transient Stability and Equal Area Criterion
key_concepts.explanation: The stability of the system following a large, sudden disturbance, such as a severe short-circuit fault. The Equal Area Criterion is a graphical method used to determine the transient stability of a Single Machine Infinite Bus (SMIB) system without formally solving the swing equation.

sections.title: Switchgear and Protection
sections.description: Apparatus and schemes used for switching, controlling, and protecting electrical circuits and equipment by isolating faulty sections.

key_concepts.explanation: The high-frequency transient voltage that appears across the contacts of a circuit breaker immediately after the arc is extinguished at zero current.

results: Buchholz Relay: A gas-actuated relay used universally for the protection of oil-immersed transformers against all internal incipient faults.
Mho Relay (Admittance Relay): Best suited for the protection of long transmission lines because it is least affected by severe power swings.
Impedance Relay: Generally utilized for the protection of medium-length transmission lines.
Reactance Relay: Highly suitable for the protection of short transmission lines, as it remains completely unaffected by arc resistance.
